tone_patterns: Formal, assurance-oriented tone that emphasizes structured integration into existing enterprise risk management
Uses cautious, forward-looking language to describe evolving practices and planned enhancements
Balances technical specificity (methods, inputs, outputs) with governance framing (oversight, decision-usefulness)
Positions limitations transparently (e.g., scope not covered in the period) while outlining next steps
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short framing paragraph stating the objective: integrating climate-related risks into existing frameworks and covering both transition and physical risk categories
Uses a lead-in sentence followed by bullet lists to explain how the framework operates in practice
Alternates between narrative explanation and enumerated components (policy, governance, regulatory alignment)
Includes a retrospective paragraph describing the reporting-period focus area, followed by a scoped list of covered sectors/areas
Introduces scenario analysis with a short contextual paragraph, then lists selected scenarios with consistent mini-definitions
Presents data sources as categorized bullets (regulatory variables, company-level data, industry data, emissions data)
Describes modelling/stress testing as a step-by-step workflow using short labeled statements per step
Closes with monitoring/prioritisation mechanisms and a phased roadmap for data/reporting improvements, then a brief concluding statement reinforcing intent and resilience
heading_patterns: Uses hierarchical numbering: main subsection number + title (e.g., section-level numbering within a chapter)
Employs numbered subheadings to structure the narrative as a process (Identification → Scenario analysis/data sources → Data sources → Monitoring/prioritisation)
Subheadings are concise noun phrases describing the disclosure topic rather than full sentences
Subheadings appear as standalone lines separating blocks of text and lists
table_patterns: No tables present in the excerpt; content that could be tabular is instead presented as categorized bullet lists and stepwise workflows
Scenario descriptions are formatted like a list with consistent labels and brief definitions, functioning as a pseudo-table without gridlines
figure_or_diagram_patterns: No figures shown; the modelling approach is conveyed as a linear process description that could be converted into a flow diagram (inputs → scenario variables → projections → outputs → assessment)
Uses labeled steps that map cleanly to boxes/arrows in a process flow visual
pdf_layout_patterns: Each page includes a running footer area with section label and page number, reinforcing navigation and context
Chapter/section identifier appears consistently near the bottom margin, separate from body text
Bulleted lists use generous line spacing and indentation to improve scanability in a PDF layout
Numbered subheadings are visually separated from preceding text, acting as anchors for multi-page continuity
Multi-page continuity is maintained by repeating the section label on each page
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses integration language: embedding climate considerations into existing policies, frameworks, and decision-making bodies
Uses governance language: oversight, regular updates, informed decision-making, alignment with regulatory expectations
Uses methodological disclosure language: scenarios selected, inputs used, modelling steps, outputs produced
Uses materiality/prioritisation language: mechanisms, thresholds, scorecards, stress testing results
Uses limitation-and-plan phrasing: acknowledges areas not covered in the period and specifies planned actions and timing in general terms
Uses decision-usefulness framing: reporting capabilities intended to provide timely information for board and senior management
evidence_presentation_patterns: References external frameworks/guidance as methodological anchors (e.g., scenario providers and supervisory guidance) without deep citation formatting
Presents evidence through structured lists of inputs, variables, and outputs rather than quantitative results
Describes analytical scope via bounded populations (e.g., top exposures) and sector groupings to demonstrate coverage logic
Explains model outputs in terms of risk-relevant indicators (e.g., ratings/credit analytics outputs) rather than raw model parameters
Uses process transparency (stepwise modelling narrative) as the primary form of substantiation
section_specific_observations: Risk management disclosure is organized as an end-to-end lifecycle: identification, scenario selection, data sourcing, modelling, prioritisation, monitoring, and planned enhancements
The section blends policy/governance controls with quantitative/analytical methods, keeping both under a single narrative thread
Physical risk is treated as a distinct workstream with explicit acknowledgement of current coverage gaps and planned tooling
Monitoring is framed as periodic reporting cycles and integration into existing risk appetite and enterprise reporting routines
things_to_avoid_copying: Any organization names, report titles, or branded policy names/acronyms
Any references to specific regulators, central banks, jurisdictions, or supervisory guidance by name
Any specific scenario names, temperature pathways, or time horizons as stated
Any specific portfolio scope definitions (e.g., exact exposure counts) or sector lists as written
Any mention of proprietary datasets, vendors, or tools
Any specific implementation dates or financial year references
Any claims of assurance, commitment, or stakeholder outcomes phrased as in the source
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Named climate risk policy and its acronym
Named external scenario framework and named supervisory guidance sources
Specific scenario labels and associated temperature outcomes/time horizons
Specific portfolio scope size and the enumerated sector categories
Named regulatory variables and detailed variable list
Mentions of proprietary market intelligence datasets and climate risk tools
Specific planned year for physical risk assessment implementation
